hook.say: This morning's paper found 215 of 392 data-loss trials hit only a reachable backup. I went back into the paper and its coverage for more.

findings.label: ORIGINAL ROWS
findings.headline: A paper reports 177 of 392 loss trials hit original rows
findings.detail: We could not find this figure on the cited arXiv page at check time.
findings.evidence: 392 permanent-loss trials of 3887, 177 with original-row loss
findings.say: First, the arXiv paper says 177 of 392 permanent-loss trials destroyed original rows, but we could not confirm that number on its page.

findings.label: HYPOTHESES
findings.headline: Preregistered hypotheses that met their decision rule
findings.detail: Four did not, including one where agents never found the credential.
findings.evidence: Three of seven preregistered hypotheses met their decision rule; post-hoc analyses are exploratory.
findings.say: Second, only three of the seven preregistered hypotheses held up. Four did not, so the conclusions are narrower than the headline suggests.

findings.label: TRIALS
findings.headline: Agent trials, all on small open-weight models
findings.detail: Six models from 4B to 35B parameters across nine engines.
findings.evidence: They ran a minimal agent with six small open-weight models (4B–12B plus a 35B MoE) across nine engines in 9,468 trials.
findings.say: Third, the study ran 9,468 trials, but only on small models up to 35 billion parameters. Larger frontier models were not part of it.

take.headline: Backups the agent can reach aren't backups
take.say: Keep backups out of your agent's reach and test your own setup. Do you use agents on databases? Comment CHECK and tell me.

sources.title: arXiv: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
ZeroHour: Study tests what limits damage when AI agents err on databases
KBlip: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?

caption:
This morning I shared a new paper on agent guardrails: in 215 of 392 data-loss trials, only a reachable backup copy was lost.

Not confirmed: the paper is said to report that 177 of those 392 trials destroyed original rows. We could not find this figure on the cited page at check time. Other data points: only 3 of 7 preregistered hypotheses met their decision rule, and all 9,468 trials used small open-weight models.

My take: measure what your agent really touches, and keep backups out of its reach.

Comment CHECK and I will DM you what I find.

Sources in the first comment.
